title: Automated microbenchmark generation from production traces for verified profile publish
creator: Marisol Chen
description: Problem statement: Current profile publishing relies on manually authored microbench suites and static sample prompts. This leads to profiles that underrepresent tail shapes and customer-weighted workloads, causing surprises in latency/cost after publish. Goal: build an automated pipeline that converts anonymized production traces into repeatable microbenchmark sequences used during model onboarding and profile verification. The pipeline must produce deterministic workloads that exercise NVidia GPU memory/KV-cache patterns and token-length distributions, output a signed performance artifact (latency/throughput/cost vectors), and record provenance for audit and rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Trace extractor can consume a 24-hour anonymized sample (S3 path) and output a compact workload spec within 2 hours
Generated microbench suites produce stable median latency within ±5% across three CI runs on the same runtime-hardware pairing
Publish pipeline ingests microbench artifact and emits a Redwood-verified profile JSON with latency, throughput, and normalized cost fields
Profile artifact includes provenance metadata: trace sample id, generator version, runtime config, and commit sha
Profiles generated by this flow are visible in the staging catalog and can be pinned to a canary rollout via Console
End-to-end pipeline has telemetry: job duration, sample size, failure rate, and a drift-score compared to last published profile
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (alpha): integrate extractor + generator and run against internal shadow traffic; store artifacts in staging-catalog (2 sprints)
Phase 2 (beta): enable for new model onboarding on dedicated infra with opt-in by model stewards; validate with canary traffic (2 sprints)
Phase 3 (GA): make generator the default for Verified Profile publishes with fallback to manual suites if generator fails; add UI controls to Console for artifact inspection (1 sprint)
Post-GA: schedule weekly sample-driven refresh jobs and enable alerting for profile drift > threshold
telemetry_contract: Emit events to perf-profile-ingest: {job_id, trace_sample_id, records_consumed, generated_sequences, run_duration_ms, generator_version, failure_reason}. Emit profile-published: {profile_id, model, runtime_anchor, median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, throughput_rps, normalized_token_cost}. All events must include customer_tier: internal|hosted|dedicated.
risks: PII leakage from traces if anonymization is incomplete — mitigation: apply deterministic hashing and S3-level access controls, add audit step
Generator creates workloads that are non-representative for low-volume customers — mitigation: support per-customer overlay and weighting policy
Flaky CI hardware leads to noisy artifacts — mitigation: require 3 independent runs and stability checks before publishing
Performance regressions in runtime due to generator targeting unusual KV patterns — mitigation: run generator on canary nodes first and instrument fallback rules
notes: This initiative sits at the intersection of Research/Applied ML (trace-to-workload heuristics), Runtime (kernel scheduling / batching fidelity), and Console (artifact UI + pinning). Engineering will own the generator and ingestion pipeline; Product will own acceptance criteria and rollout gating. We will coordinate with Solutions for early customer trials and Legal for trace handling controls.
